creator: Asbjørn Munk, Stefano Cerri, Jakob Ambsdorf, Julia Machnio, Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias, Vardan Nersesjan, Christian Hedeager Krag, Peirong Liu, Pablo Rocamora García, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi, Mikael Boesen, Michael Eriksen Benros, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, Mads Nielsen (University of Copenhagen)
description: FOMO60K is a large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, and others), and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies. It is intended to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging at scale.

rai:dataBiases: Source datasets are often curated for specific diseases or patient populations and typically follow homogeneous imaging protocols with limited pathological variability. FOMO60K was designed to address this by aggregating from 16 diverse sources spanning clinical- and research-grade imaging, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability including large brain anomalies.
rai:dataCollection: FOMO60K was aggregated from 16 publicly available brain MRI datasets: MGH Wild, SOOP, BraTS-GEN, OASIS1, OASIS2, MSD Braintumor, IXI, NIMH, DLBS, IDEAS, ARC, MBSR, UCLA, QTAB, NKI, and AOMIC ID1000. The dataset spans both clinical- and research-grade imaging, includes multiple MRI sequences (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, T1ce, PD, SWI, GRE), and captures anatomical and pathological diversity including scans with large brain anomalies.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Brain MRI scans from 16 publicly available datasets, including T1-weighted, T2-weighted, FLAIR, DWI, T1ce (contrast-enhanced), Proton Density (PD), Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging (SWI), and Gradient Echo (GRE) sequences. Scans originate from both clinical and research settings, covering a wide range of subjects and pathologies.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Subjects were shuffled to protect privacy and prevent easy identification of dataset sources. All MRI scans are stored in NIfTI-compressed format and organized using a standardized directory structure with unique subject identifiers (sub_X) and session labels (ses_Y). Scans are named according to sequence type; multiple scans of the same sequence are enumerated; scans with unavailable sequence information are generically named scan_X.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing comprised three main steps: (1) reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation; (2) affine co-registration using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.1 with default parameters, aligning scans within each session to the image with the highest spatial resolution; (3) skull-stripping using SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1), applied only when images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features. For DWI scans in 4D format: b=0 volumes were extracted separately; for the b=1000 shell, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on gradient directions most closely aligned with canonical x, y, z axes (via cosine similarity), then averaged to produce a single representative 3D image.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.
rai:dataUseCases: Development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning (SSL) methods in medical imaging at scale; SSL pretraining and fine-tuning for brain MRI analysis; neuroimaging research requiring large-scale, heterogeneous data.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1) — a deep learning-based brain segmentation tool used to generate segmentation masks for skull-stripping. FreeSurfer 7.4.1 mri_coreg command used for affine co-registration.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: All scans have been skull-stripped or defaced to protect subject anonymity. Subjects have been shuffled to prevent easy identification of dataset sources. The dataset contains brain MRI scans of human subjects, but direct identifiers have been removed through defacing or skull-stripping.
